The figure below shows the graph of $f'$, the derivative of $f$, with domain $-3 \le x \le 9$. The graph of $f'$ has horizontal tangents at $x = 2$ and $x = 4$ and a corner at $x = 6$.

Is $f$ continuous? Explain.

figures.alt: The graph of $f'$ on $-3\le x\le 9$ (closed dots at both endpoints). It starts at $x=-3$ well below the x-axis, rises and crosses the x-axis at $x=-2$, and keeps rising to a smooth local maximum (horizontal tangent) at $x=2$. It then falls to touch the x-axis at $x=4$ (a smooth minimum with $f'(4)=0$, staying above the axis on both sides), rises to a sharp corner peak at $x=6$, then falls and crosses the x-axis at $x=7$. For $7<x\le 9$ it is below the x-axis and ends at $x=9$ at a negative value (about half as far below the axis as at $x=-3$). So $f'>0$ on $(-2,7)$ except $f'(4)=0$, and $f'<0$ on $[-3,-2)$ and $(7,9]$.
